full_text_zh:
[P1] 去海边玩
撰文/蔡欣颖 插画/吕育真

[P2] 去海边玩
撰文/蔡欣颖 插画/吕育真

浙江出版联合集团
浙江少年儿童出版社
2/12

[P3] 今年暑假，爸爸妈妈带小勇去海边玩。
海边人好多，好热闹哦！
有人在挖沙坑、堆沙堡，
还有人在抓螃蟹、打水仗，
大家都玩得好开心。

阿宝哥小教室
在堆沙的时候，要在沙里加一点点水，
缩小沙与沙之间的空隙，增加沙和沙的
紧密度，堆出来的沙堡才会更坚固哦！

[P4] 妈妈牵着小勇的手走向海边，走过沙滩时，小勇发现沙子好烫啊！
他们赶紧跑向海边，有海水的地方，沙子就不烫了，终于可以尽情地玩了！
试一试，走在沙滩上和走在有海水冲过的沙子上，
感觉有什么不一样呢？
阿宝哥小教室
因为太阳的照射，沙滩上的沙子吸收了很多热量，所以当我们走在沙滩上时会觉得脚底很烫。但冰凉的海水会带走沙子上的热量，因此，被海浪冲到的沙子就不会烫了哦！

[P5] 咦，沙滩上怎么有好多小洞？还有好多小沙球？
哇，仔细一看，还有好多小螃蟹和寄居蟹在跑来跑去！
为什么螃蟹要堆沙球呢？
这些是螃蟹吃过的沙球，也有人称它为“拟粪”。螃蟹会滤出沙子里的浮游性植物、鱼虾的卵等来当作食物。
我们会从沙里把可以吃的食物筛选出来吃掉，剩下的沙团再吐出来丢到一边，这样一来，就不会重复捡来吃了。
螃蟹的脚长在身体的两侧，每只脚的关节只能上下运动，不能左右转动，所以，螃蟹只能横着走，不能往前直着走哦！
螃蟹为什么会横着走呢？
● 寄居蟹是螃蟹，还是海螺？
寄居蟹是螃蟹的远房亲戚，由于寄居蟹的腹部很脆弱，需要用壳来保护自己，因此，它会把海螺死掉后留下的空壳当作自己的家。所以说，寄居蟹其实是螃蟹，而不是海螺！

[P6] 小勇追着螃蟹跑啊跑，却发现沙滩上有些小洞会喷水。小勇挖开洞穴一看，居然有蛤蜊躲在里面。没想到，除了螃蟹外，沙滩上竟然还有好多其他小动物。

蛤蜊
多数的蛤类栖于浅水水域，埋在水底泥沙中免受海浪打击。

贝壳
死掉的贝类留下的硬壳。

藤壶
左边像小火山口一样的东西其实是藤壶，藤壶经常被误认成贝类，它的吸附能力非常强，可以黏附在岩石和浮木上生活。

螃蟹
螃蟹会在沙滩上挖洞保护自己，一旦遇到危险，它们就会赶紧躲回洞里，等安全了再出来。

[P7] “奇怪，为什么海边的小动物都要躲在壳里或沙子里呢？”
妈妈说，因为它们要保护自己不被鸟吃掉。

海鸥
海鸥身体下半部的羽毛就像雪一样洁白，善于飞翔。

小燕鸥
一种成群出现在河口、海岸、沼泽及内陆湖泊等地的鸟类。

滨鹬（yù）
一种出现在海边和河口的鸟类，它们会用黑色长嘴挖掘沙地或泥地，找出沙或泥里的小动物来吃。

东方环颈鸻（héng）
东方环颈鸻颈部有一圈白色羽毛，身体颜色很接近沙地的颜色，使它不容易被敌人发现。

[P8] 认识特殊的海边生物

藤壶
一种附着在海边岩石上的一簇簇灰白色、有石灰质外壳的动物。它们不但能附着在礁石上，还能附着在船体上，而且极其牢固。

滨鹬
通常在冬季向南迁移至各大洲的海岸过冬，常沿着潮线奔跑觅食。觅食时，会急速将嘴插入泥滩中取食无脊椎动物或昆虫，有时也会在浅滩处觅食。

小燕鸥
身长约28厘米，背部灰色，脚橘黄色，头顶至后颈、过眼线为黑色，头至颈部、胸以下为白色。常发出连续、尖锐且急促的“嘎啊——嘎啊——”的叫声。

东方环颈鸻
嘴巴是黑色的，脖子短，头有些扁，腹部至尾下均为白色，脚为黄色。

[P9] 妈妈，好奇怪，为什么我的脸上有很多白白的颗粒？
因为海边的浪花激起时，会有少数的盐巴飞散在空中，所以会咸咸的哦！
太阳快下山了，小鸟们也都要回家了。妈妈帮小勇擦干身体，洗好脸。
“海边好好玩哦！”小勇说，“下次我一定要再来玩！”
我好像被晒伤了，好痛哦！
到海边一定要注意防晒，还要记得补充水分哦！
阿宝哥小教室
海水里有盐，海水经过太阳暴晒，水分蒸发后，盐就会被结晶出来了。
给爸妈的悄悄话
炎炎夏日，小朋友最喜欢去玩水了。家长不妨趁着夏天天气热，带孩子到海边玩，不但可以满足孩子爱玩水的心理，还可以引导孩子认识海边的各种生物，感受大海的魅力。
9/12

[P10] 海边好好玩
小螃蟹，横着走，
走到东，走到西，
边吐泡泡，边吃东西，
全身不会脏兮兮。

寄居蟹，爱乱跑，
跑到东，跑到西，
请问你在找什么东西？
是找贝壳，
还是发亮的水晶？

海边好好玩，
沙滩真温暖，海水好冰凉，
还有许多海鸥在飞翔。

给爸妈的悄悄话
这首儿歌在乐曲创作上使用了三连音，使旋律
听起来有摇摆、轻松的感觉。编曲则使用打击乐器
做衬底，以木琴、铁琴和铃鼓等乐器来伴奏，爸妈
可以和小朋友一起在歌曲中寻找这些声音，仔细听
听它们出现在歌曲中的哪些地方。另外，在塑料
瓶、铁罐或铝罐内装入细沙、小石头，做成手摇乐
器——沙铃，就能制造出海浪的音效，可以跟着旋
律一起演奏哦！

full_text_en:
[P1] Going to the Beach
Written by Cai Xinying  Illustrated by Lü Yuzhen

[P2] Go to the Seaside
Written by Cai Xinying  Illustrated by Lü Yuzhen

Zhejiang Publishing United Group
Zhejiang Children's Publishing House
2/12

[P3] This summer vacation, Mom and Dad took Xiao Yong to the beach.
The beach was crowded and so lively!
Some people were digging sand pits and building sandcastles,
while others were catching crabs and playing water fights.
Everyone was having a great time.

A-Bao-Ge's Little Classroom
When building sandcastles, add a little water to the sand,
reduce the gaps between sand particles, increase the density of the sand,
and your sandcastle will be much more solid!

[P4] Mom holds Xiao Yong's hand and walks toward the seaside. When they walk across the beach, Xiao Yong finds the sand is so hot!
They quickly run toward the seaside. Where there is seawater, the sand is no longer hot. Finally, they can play to their heart's content!
Try it: walk on the beach and on the sand washed by seawater.
How do they feel different?
Abao Brother's Classroom
Because of the sun's rays, the sand on the beach absorbs a lot of heat. So when we walk on the beach, our feet feel very hot. But the cool seawater takes away the heat from the sand. Therefore, the sand washed by waves won't be hot anymore!

[P5] Hey, why are there so many little holes and sand balls on the beach?
Wow, looking closely, there are lots of little crabs and hermit crabs running around!
Why do crabs make sand balls?
These are sand balls left after crabs eat. Some people call them 'pseudofeces'. Crabs filter out floating plants, fish eggs, and shrimp eggs from the sand to eat.
We filter out edible food from the sand, eat it, and then spit out the leftover sand balls to the side. This way, we won't pick up the same sand again.
Crabs' legs grow on both sides of their bodies. Each leg's joint can only move up and down, not left or right. So, crabs can only walk sideways, not straight forward!
Why do crabs walk sideways?
● Is a hermit crab a crab or a snail?
Hermit crabs are distant relatives of crabs. Since hermit crabs have very fragile abdomens, they need shells to protect themselves. Therefore, they use empty shells left behind by dead snails as their homes. So, hermit crabs are actually crabs, not snails!

[P6] Xiaoyong chased the crabs around, but noticed some small holes on the beach were spouting water. When he dug one open, he found clams hiding inside. He didn't expect that, besides crabs, there were many other small animals on the beach.

Clams
Most clams live in shallow waters, buried in the muddy sand at the bottom to avoid being hit by waves.

Shells
Hard shells left behind by dead shellfish.

Barnacles
The things on the left that look like small volcanic craters are actually barnacles. Barnacles are often mistaken for shellfish. They have very strong adhesive ability and can attach to rocks and floating wood to live.

Crabs
Crabs dig holes in the sand to protect themselves. When they encounter danger, they quickly hide back in their holes and come out again only when it's safe.

[P7] "Strange, why do all the little animals by the seaside hide in shells or sand?"
Mom said, "Because they need to protect themselves from being eaten by birds.

Gull
The feathers on the lower half of a gull's body are as white as snow, and it is good at flying.

Little Tern
A type of bird that appears in flocks at river mouths, coastlines, marshes, and inland lakes.

Plover (yù)
A type of bird found at seashores and river mouths. They use their long black beaks to dig into sand or mud to find small animals to eat.

Oriental Plover (héng)
The Oriental Plover has a ring of white feathers around its neck. Its body color closely matches the sand, making it hard for enemies to spot.

[P8] Getting to Know Special Seashore Creatures

Barnacles
A type of animal that attaches in clusters to rocks along the seashore, with grayish-white, calcareous shells. They can not only attach to rocks, but also to ship hulls, and are extremely firm.

Dunlin
Usually migrates southward to coastlines across continents in winter, often running along the tide line to forage. When feeding, it quickly inserts its beak into mudflats to eat invertebrates or insects, and sometimes forages in shallow waters.

Little Tern
About 28 cm in length, with gray back, orange-yellow legs, black crown to nape and eye stripe, and white from head to neck and below the chest. It often emits a continuous, sharp, and urgent "kak-kaa..." call.

Oriental Plover
Has a black beak, short neck, slightly flat head, white belly to undertail, and yellow legs.

[P9] Mom, it's strange, why are there so many white particles on my face?
Because when the waves splash at the seaside, some salt flies into the air, so it tastes salty!
The sun is setting, and the birds are going home. Mom helps Xiao Yong dry his body and wash his face.
"The seaside is so much fun!" Xiao Yong says, "Next time, I definitely want to come back and play!"
I think I got sunburned, it hurts so much!
Remember to protect yourself from the sun and stay hydrated when you go to the seaside!
Abao Brother's Little Classroom
Seawater contains salt. When seawater is exposed to the sun, the water evaporates, and the salt crystallizes.
Tips for Parents
In hot summer, children love to play in water. Parents can take advantage of the hot weather to bring children to the seaside. Not only can it satisfy children's love for water play, but it can also guide them to learn about various seaside creatures and experience the charm of the sea.
9/12

[P10] By the Sea, So Much Fun
Little crab, walking sideways,
Walking east, walking west,
Bubbling and eating,
Never getting dirty.

Hermit crab, loves to run,
Running east, running west,
What are you looking for?
Are you looking for shells,
or shiny crystals?

By the sea, so much fun,
Sand is warm, seawater is cool,
And many seagulls are flying.

Tips for Parents
This children's song uses triplets in its composition, making the melody sound swinging and relaxed. The arrangement uses percussion instruments as a base, accompanied by xylophone, metallophone, and tambourine. Parents can listen with their children to find these sounds in the song and pay attention to where they appear. Also, fill plastic bottles, tin cans, or aluminum cans with fine sand or small stones to make a shaker — a sand bell — which can create the sound of waves, and play along with the melody!

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页是绘本的封面，标题为《去海边玩》，展示了孩子们在沙滩上堆沙堡、戏水的欢乐场景，背景有海浪、遮阳伞和海鸟，画面充满夏日海边的童趣。
[P2] 本页为绘本《去海边玩》的扉页，显示了书名、作者和插画师信息，下方有一只卡通螃蟹插图，底部标注了出版社和页码。
[P3] 本页描绘了小勇和家人在海边游玩的场景，沙滩上人们在挖沙坑、堆沙堡、抓螃蟹和打水仗，画面充满欢乐气氛。右下角的‘阿宝哥小教室’介绍了堆沙堡时加水能使沙堡更坚固的小知识。
[P4] 小勇和妈妈在沙滩上发现沙子很烫，于是跑向有海水的地方避暑，画面中还有其他孩子在海边玩耍，右下角的‘阿宝哥小教室’解释了沙滩沙子变烫和海水降温的科学原理。
[P5] 小勇和妈妈在沙滩上发现许多小洞和沙球，原来是螃蟹和寄居蟹在活动。妈妈向小勇解释螃蟹堆沙球的原因和寄居蟹的习性，同时页面通过对话和插图科普了螃蟹横着走的原理以及寄居蟹与海螺的区别。
[P6] 小勇在沙滩上追螃蟹时，发现有小洞喷水，挖开后发现是蛤蜊，进而了解到沙滩上还有藤壶、贝壳和螃蟹等多种小动物，并通过图文科普了它们的习性和特征。
[P7] 小勇在沙滩上观察海边鸟类，向妈妈提问为什么小动物躲在壳或沙里，妈妈解释是为了躲避鸟类捕食。页面同时科普了海鸥、小燕鸥、滨鹬和东方环颈鸻的特征与习性。
[P8] 本页介绍了四种特殊的海边生物：藤壶、滨鹬、小燕鸥和东方环颈鸻，通过图文并茂的方式描述了它们的外形特征和生活习性。
[P9] 夕阳西下，小勇和妈妈在沙滩上准备回家，小勇脸上有盐粒，妈妈解释是海水蒸发后留下的盐结晶。画面中其他孩子有的晒伤，有的补充水分，妈妈提醒注意防晒和补水。页面通过“阿宝哥小教室”科普盐结晶原理，并在“给爸妈的悄悄话”中建议家长带孩子玩水、认识海洋生物。
[P10] 本页以儿歌形式描绘了海边的欢乐场景，通过小螃蟹和寄居蟹的活动展现海洋生物的趣味，同时配有插图和‘给爸妈的悄悄话’，介绍歌曲的音乐特点及亲子互动建议。
[P11] 画面描绘了小男孩小勇在沙滩上快乐奔跑，旁边有妈妈和几只海鸥，沙滩上有小螃蟹和寄居蟹，前景是盛开的牵牛花，整体呈现海边嬉戏的欢乐场景。
[P12] 本页为广告页，展示Tiger Lee品牌标识和宣传语，介绍其提供高品质电子绘本资源，并附有淘宝二维码和网址，承诺每月免费更新。
